models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light easterly air holds through tomorrow - Panarea to Filicudi is an early, downwind motor-sail in under 1 ft of sea.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the Aeolians: all three atmospheric models (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, ECMWF AIFS and ICON-2i, all 06 Oct 12Z) keep winds in the 3-8 kt band through Wednesday, backing from SSE overnight to E during the day. Seas stay small - MFWAM (06 Oct 00Z) and ECMWF WAM (12Z) agree on total wave around 0.7-1.0 ft at Panarea with 0.6-0.7 ft of ESE swell. The pattern turns more active by Friday 09 Oct, when the models bring thunderstorms and NW-N wind into the Salina-Portorosa window; nothing in this payload tells us about the synoptic driver behind that, only the end result.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Recommended berth is the San Pietro buoy field (shelter score 0.83); Drautto and Cala Zimmari score effectively the same, so the choice does not matter tonight. Expect SSE 7-8 kt with ESE swell at 0.7 ft - San Pietro is open through 030-180°, so it is exposed to that direction, but the strength is trivial. One figure to note: the consensus shows a gust to 21.6 kt at Panarea around midnight against a 7.6 kt mean, an interval-maximum from the gust-publishing models; if that verifies as real squally air rather than model artefact, boats on the buoys will feel it as a short swell-and-snatch, not a reason to move.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: By 06:00 Panarea is forecast at 4.2 kt from the S with 0.7 ft wave and 0.6 ft swell - benign. Recommended departure for Panarea to Filicudi is 06:00, giving SSE 5 kt at 112° TWA, a broad reach, with 0.8 ft of sea and a 4-hour run to a 10:00 arrival. Every window from 06:00 through 14:00 is rated go, with wind 5-7 kt and wave never above 1.0 ft, so the window is effectively all day; the only argument for leaving early is arriving before the afternoon E filling in to 7 kt puts you dead downwind and under power.

passage_notes.note: Go at 06:00. SSE-E 5-7 kt, wave 0.8-1.0 ft, broad reach early turning to a dead run (TWA 158-175°) from 10:00 onward. Gusts to 13-15 kt appear against a 5 kt mean - interval maxima in light air, reported but not treated as a caution. Plan on motoring part of 28 nm.

Go, all windows. Wind 3-6 kt SSW backing to E, wave 0.5-0.7 ft. After midday the wind is on the nose (TWA 9° then 2°) - that is a motoring leg if you leave late. Gust spikes to 17-19 kt against a 6 kt mean show in the gust models; worth watching but not currently a caution.

Only the 06:00 departure is rated go (NW 5 kt, wave 0.9 ft, dead downwind). Every window from 08:00 onward is flagged no-go on forecast thunderstorms, with wave building to 1.8 ft and gusts to 26 kt by the 14:00 slot. If this holds, it is a dawn start or a day in Salina.

cautions: Thunderstorms are forecast in the Salina-Portorosa window from 08:00 Friday 09 Oct onward - all four later windows are rated no-go. Re-brief Thursday evening.

Models disagree at Stromboli for 06:00 Wednesday: 3.3 to 10.5 kt. That is the only point in the payload where the spread exceeds 6 kt, and it does not sit on tomorrow's track, but it flags some uncertainty in the overnight SSE.

Gust-to-mean ratios are large everywhere in this light air (e.g. 21.6 kt gust on a 7.6 kt mean at Panarea tonight). These are interval maxima from IFS and ICON-2i, not sustained values - treat them as a reason to stay rigged conservatively, not as a forecast of wind.
The 10 Oct Portorosa berth entry lists 16.0 kt wind with a 10.5 kt gust, which is internally inconsistent. Do not plan on that figure; it needs a fresher run.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i (all 06 Oct 12Z) agree closely on tomorrow's light easterlies and the stability record shows only 1.2 kt mean run-to-run shift at 12-24 h lead, but the Stromboli 3.3-10.5 kt spread and Friday's convective signal keep this short of high.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
